market_holds: Options (sealed 18:10 UTC at spot $15.155): event-implied move 14.8%, front straddle 16.2%, skew balanced (+0.3 vol pts), put/call OI 0.41. Usual move: median |reaction| 13.1% over 8 prints, 7 of 8 down (-21.9% on 2026-08-06). Run-up: 5d +20.8%, 20d +26.9%. Almost all of it came TODAY: a Yahoo daily bar shows 11-06 close $12.93 and $15.18 intraday on 11-09 (+17%) on 40.5m shares against a 20d average of 15.5m, with no company news, only 'low bar' and 'sector optimism' explanations (Investing.com, BigGo, 24/7 Wall St, all 2026-11-09). The stock is still about 66% below its 52-week high and 27% above its low. Consensus: Q3 revenue ~$650-657m, which is the company's own floor (guide 'at least $650m', adj. EBITDA ~$160m, 8-K 2026-08-06). EPS $0.25, cut from ~$0.50 ninety days ago with 17 downward revisions in 30 days (Yahoo/24/7 2026-11-09). Implied Q4 consensus $692-699m: -18% y/y against $847m, +6-7.5% sequential. Short interest 83.1m shares at 10/15 settlement, about 18% of the ~473m shares outstanding (Nasdaq API). Sell-side: BNP Underperform $10, HSBC Reduce $10, Citi Sell $11 (all Aug-2026). The line the stock trades on is the Q4 guide.
view: The print turns on the Q4 guide against an implied consensus of roughly $692-699m. Q3 itself will probably clear the $650m floor. A new CFO set that floor ('assumes no meaningful recovery'), it predates the 15% headcount cut, and Magnite's Nov-4 print shows midterm political spend running about 3x its own forecast, mostly in CTV, with Q4 political larger than Q3. But a beat on a floor that consensus already sits on is not news. The Q4 number can be read two ways from the same public data. Seasonally it looks easy: Q3 to Q4 was +14.6% in 2025, and October is the political peak. On the trajectory of the business it does not: the sequential shortfall against 2025 has widened every quarter (Q1 -1.8 pts, Q2 -8.9 pts, Q3 -15.6 pts at the floor). Consensus at +6.4% sequential already assumes that shortfall roughly halves. The 10-Q says existing clients are spending less, and Amazon's fee pressure and agency friction are structural. A new CFO who missed his predecessor's Q2 floor has every reason to guide Q4 conservatively, so a guide at or a little below the implied consensus is quite plausible. On top of that, the stock rose 17% today on no news, so part of a relief rally is already in the price; a merely in-line guide could fade it. I cannot show either reading is unpriced. I lean slightly down because of the same-day squeeze and the trajectory, not strongly enough to recommend anything.

recommendation.reason: The decisive number is the Q4 guide against an implied ~$692-699m consensus. Seasonality plus political points above it; the widening sequential shortfall and a conservative new CFO point at or below it. Today's 17% no-news rally into the print leaves the price neither clearly behind nor clearly ahead. No mechanism clears 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 floor at or above ~$720m with management saying existing clients are spending again would make this a clear up-move given ~18% of shares short; a floor below ~$680m would make it a clear down-move that gives back today's rally and more.

self_critique: Leaning down may be wrong. 18% of shares are short, consensus has been cut 17 times in a month, the stock trades near 14x forward with ~$1.1bn net cash, and the new CFO's first full guide could kitchen-sink Q3 so that Q3 and EBITDA beat comfortably. Political CTV spend was a record, and October is in Q4. A Q4 floor of $700m+ would easily squeeze shorts further despite today's run. Against the up case: today's no-news +17% is exactly the kind of positioning that turns an in-line print into a sell-off, and 7 of the last 8 reactions were down.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line: the Q4 guide) and P3's 'freshest data first' (Magnite's Nov-4 print, same-day tape) helped most; my own sequential arithmetic was the most informative piece.
